page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is an ARM64-based compute-optimized server powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1d cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

This server comes with 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, offering high-speed local disk access directly attached to the instance. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In benchmark testing, the c6gd.2xlarge demonstrates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12,133.14 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,364.0. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached reads at 473.11 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads and writes reach 116.89 GB/sec and 50.84 GB/sec respectively. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 20.32 GB/sec. Database operations and web serving are solid, with Redis SET operations handling 9.43 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 9.78 GB/sec.

The ARM64 architecture and dedicated physical cores offer a cost-efficient alternative to x86-based compute instances, delivering balanced resource density for multi-threaded workloads. Given its compute-to-memory ratio and local NVMe SSD storage, this instance is well-suited for distributed data processing, software compilation, static web serving, and database workloads that benefit from low-latency local scratch space. It is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large language model inference.
